title: Filter the home claims dashboard and inspect its summaries
prerequisites: Sign in; this screen is protected by the application's authentication guard.
Dashboard cards and charts depend on configured dashboard setup and the current user's role.
steps: Choose Encounter Date or Received Date under Sorting.
Optionally select one or more Facilities and Payers; set From Date and To Date, or use Day, Week, or Month.
Select the search button to refresh the dashboard; Clear Filter removes the selections and restores the date sorting to Encounter Date.

Open a count-bearing summary card to view its detailed summary. The detailed panel can switch between facility and payer summaries and the Received, Unclaimed, Claimed, Accepted, and Rejected categories.
When the Payment Reconcile Summary is available, review claim, received, unapplied, adjusted-percent, approved, and settled totals.
notes: The Task filter is present in the component model but is commented out in the current template; do not advise users that they can select tasks here.
Dashboard setup determines which information boxes and graphs appear. Coder and reviewer roles are handled separately, and a user with no configured widgets may see a default page instead.
The independent DashboardModule has a component route, but AppRoutingModule does not mount it. /dashboard is therefore not verified as reachable in this UI; /home is the active dashboard entry.
Dashboard values depend on configured data and are not guarantees of payment posting or external-system status.

title: Search payment collections and open a payment record
prerequisites: Sign in with access to Payment Collection.
steps: In the collection filters, optionally select Payer and Facility.

Set Claim Period Start and Claim Period End, and Pay. Date From and Pay. Date To. These four date fields are initialized to the previous claim period and current payment period and are required by the form.
Select Search to refresh the collection list. If the start date is later than the end date, the component moves the end date forward to the start date.
Use Reset Filter to restore the initial dates and clear payer, facility, and transaction-reference criteria; the list is searched again.
Select a payment card in the left list to load its details. Use Search Transaction Reference in that list and press Enter to narrow the displayed records.
notes: Facility options are loaded for a fixed facility-group identifier in the current component; available options can depend on configuration.
The page also contains actions whose availability depends on permissions and record status; see the recording, reconciliation, and verification guidance.
Search results and record availability depend on current data and service responses.

title: Record a manual payment collection
prerequisites: Open Payment Collection and have the required record-new-payment permission.
Use the payer, facility, payment period, payment date, mode, and references relevant to the synthetic/test payment you intend to enter.
steps: Select Record New Payment to open the form.
Complete Facility Name, Payer Name, From Date, To Date, Payment Transaction On, Received Amount, Transaction Reference, Payment Mode, and Payee Reference; these are required.
Ensure Received Amount is greater than zero. If From Date is later than To Date, the form adjusts To Date to match From Date.
Optionally add Remarks or attach one PDF or image file. The client accepts listed image formats and PDF up to 5 MB.
Select Save. If the transaction reference is already used, inspect the warning and choose whether to continue; after the request succeeds, the form closes and the collection list refreshes.
notes: The UI warns about a duplicate Transaction Reference but lets the user confirm continuation; this is not evidence that the reference is globally unique.
The file check is performed in the UI; do not infer server-side retention or successful payment from the file selection alone.
Save is permission-gated. Availability of payer, facility, and payment mode options depends on configured lookup data; backend request success is environment-dependent.

title: Apply a payment collection to claims
prerequisites: Open an existing payment collection record.
The collection must not be deactivated; reconciliation is permission-gated.
steps: Select the payment record and review its received amount, unapplied amount, status, and claim details.
For a pending record with no adjustment details, select Reconcile Payments.
Review the claims returned for the payment, select an available adjustment type, and enter its percentage when that adjustment requires one.
Select Add to submit the adjustment. Reopen or refresh the record and review the claim list and settled-claim totals.
notes: The UI disables adjustment choices when the amount basis used by that choice is zero and disables Add when there are no claims to reconcile.
The adjustment types are supplied by the backend; their business definitions are not hard-coded in the UI.
Submitting a reconciliation request does not guarantee settlement; confirm the resulting status and amounts in the updated record.

title: Verify, deactivate, attach evidence, or transfer unapplied payment funds
prerequisites: Open the relevant payment collection record.
The relevant action permission is required; state and permission control the available buttons.
steps: For a pending payment with claim details, select Verify and confirm the prompt.
For a pending payment, select Deactivate and confirm if it should no longer be active.
For a pending payment, select Attachment to add a file; confirm replacement if an attachment already exists.
For a verified payment with an adjustment type and a positive Unapplied Amount, select Transfer Unapplied Amount, then choose Transfer to Other or Transfer Within.
When a transfer form opens, complete the required payment fields and select Transfer; the form carries forward payment details and disables some inherited fields.
For a verified payment with details, inspect Issue Payment Notes. The Issue Notice to NPhies option is restricted to automatic records; an Issue Notice to ERP menu item is also shown.
notes: The transfer control is only rendered for eligible verified records with a positive unapplied amount and permission. Facility selection differs between within-facility and other-facility transfer modes.
The UI's Issue Notice to ERP entry has no click handler in the current template; its operational behavior is unverified. Do not promise delivery to either external system.
A verification, deactivation, attachment upload, or transfer request may be denied or fail based on server-side permissions, validation, or service availability. Confirm the resulting record.

title: Search, acknowledge, inspect, and export received NPHIES payments
prerequisites: Sign in with access to the Payment Received screen.
Payer and Facility lookup data must be available to use those optional filters.
steps: Enter a Payment Bundle Identifier or Claim Identifier, or provide a complete Period From/Period To pair or Payment From/Payment To pair; the initial search dates default to the previous month.
Optionally filter by Facility, Payer, Status (Pending or Acknowledged), and Payment Type (Payment or Advance). Use Search to load matching Nphies Payments or Reset to clear filters.
Select a row to expand its claim details. Use the row's view action to inspect the available payment response or log.
For pending/unacknowledged entries, select one or more rows and choose Issue Notice To Nphies; acknowledged rows cannot be selected for another notice.
Select Download Excel to export the current filter result.
notes: The UI rejects missing search criteria and partial date ranges. Supply both ends of a range, or use an identifier; the component also caps normal list paging at 100 records per page and loads additional pages while scrolling.
Issue Notice To Nphies calls a payment-received update operation. Whether an external acknowledgement is delivered or accepted depends on backend and integration behavior.
The table also contains a hidden Post Payment action; it is not an active visible workflow in the current template.

Export includes payment bundle, bank name, payment identifiers, period/payment dates, payer, facility, claim count, amount, type, outcome, status, and disposition. Export/service success depends on current data and connectivity.

title: Find saved payment reconciliations
prerequisites: Sign in with access to Payment Reconciliation.
steps: On Collections, choose Facility Name, Payer Name, Period From, and Period To. All four fields are required for Search.
Select Search to list reconciliations for those criteria; if Period From is later than Period To, the end date is moved to the start date.
Review each row's reconciliation number, facility, payer, date range, status, and created date.
Select the row's view action to open its reconciliation detail. Use Record New to open a new reconciliation.
notes: Facility and payer choices come from lookup services. Results and displayed status names are backend-provided.
The search uses the current filter values and does not promise a result for every date range.

title: Build and save a new period reconciliation
prerequisites: Sign in with permission to create a reconciliation.
Identify the Facility, Payer, and period to reconcile.
steps: Open Record New from the reconciliation list, or open /payment-reconciliation/reconcile directly.
Choose Facility Name and Payer Name and set Period From and Period To; all are required for a new reconciliation.
Select Search to fetch period results. Review the displayed submitted, approved, rejected, payment, and unapplied amount totals and the period detail rows.
When the summary contains at least one period row, select Save and confirm the prompt.
After the request completes, the UI loads the saved record by UUID; review its reconciliation number, status, payer, facility, period, and audit timestamps.
notes: The new-record view populates results through the advance search; a saved record is loaded by the query parameter uuid, which changes the screen from new to view mode.
An empty result does not enable Save. Saving and subsequent details are server-dependent; verify the saved UUID-backed record.

title: Review and progress a saved reconciliation
prerequisites: Open an existing reconciliation by selecting its row from the list.
Actions are conditional on reconciliation status, user permissions, and whether reconciliation detail rows exist.
steps: Review the saved header, audit timestamps, period totals, and detail rows; use View Actual Reconcile Values to inspect the original summary amounts.
For a Pending reconciliation with detail rows, use Verify and confirm. For a Verified reconciliation, Approve and Reject are shown only when the user-approval check permits them.
Use DeActivate only while the record is Pending; confirm before the status change.

For a Pending reconciliation, use Override to enter supported summary adjustments or Credit Note to apply a positive amount. Review the existing override or credit-note history before replacing or discarding an existing credit note.
For Verified or DeActivated records, use Override History when available. Select Print to open the reconciliation report.
notes: The UI displays Submitted, Approved, Rejected, Payment, and Unapplied values as net, VAT, and total; override calculation and edit/delete availability depend on the selected row and permissions.
Credit-note entry requires an amount greater than zero unless discarding an existing credit note. A replacement/discard may prompt for confirmation.
The UI enables Approve/Reject based on Verified status and an approval-status service response; this behavior is user/configuration conditional.
A successful click is not proof of final approval, external settlement, or downstream posting. Recheck status and audit details after each operation.

title: Create or update a payer profile
prerequisites: Sign in with access to Payer setup; save and edit actions may be permission-limited.
Have the payer's authoritative configuration details available.
steps: Open the payer list at /payer/payer and use its add action to create a profile, or select an existing payer to edit.
Enter Payer Name, Payer Name Arabic, Email Address, Country, State, City, Claim Type, Payer Type, and License Number; these are required by the form.
Optionally complete contact details, address, company URL, tax details, authorized-person data, registration date, and external code.
Set the appropriate flags such as Taxable, Is Active, Is TPA, Is Managed by TPA, Shadow Billing, or DRG only when they apply to the payer configuration.
Select Save. Review the success/error message and return to the payer list.
notes: State and City are dependent on Country. Email must be valid; numeric telephone, fax, postal, and zip inputs are length/pattern validated. License Number is limited to 70 characters.
Existing-profile update versus new-profile creation is determined by the selected payer record; do not assume configuration flags enable an external connection.
Payer endpoints and related permissions are backend-managed; successful save does not verify payer integration.

title: Set up a payer policy
prerequisites: Create or identify the payer first; policy is associated with a payer.
Sign in with edit permission for payer policies.
steps: Open Payer Policy and select the add action, or open an existing policy for editing.
Select Payer, then fill Policy Name, Policy Name Arabic, Policy No, Expiry Date, and External Code; all are required.
Policy No must contain only letters and digits. Optionally enter Remarks, Insurance Nhic, and a TPA payer if one is available.
Select Save and review the response before returning to the policy list.
notes: Payer is disabled while editing an existing policy; the UI binds available TPA payers after the payer is selected.
Payer and policy lists expose search by Payer Name and External Code. Policy status is configured by the policy form's active flag.
This workflow configures payer policy data; it does not establish that a payer contract, enrollment, or external connection is active.

title: Create a payer policy class and validity period
prerequisites: The payer and its policy must already exist.
Sign in with permission to maintain policy classes.
steps: Open Payer Policy Class and select the add action, or select a class to edit.
Select Payer and then Policy; the policy choices are loaded for the selected payer.
Enter Policy Class Name, Policy Class Name Arabic, Valid From, Valid To, and External Code; these fields are required.
Optionally enter Remarks and select Active as appropriate.
Select Save and check the response.
notes: Payer and Policy selections are disabled for an existing class. Both validity dates are required; the date picker sets a minimum date, but the form does not establish that the range order is valid on the server.
Use the listed parent payer and policy records; the UI does not itself document coverage rules.

title: Create or maintain a facility group
prerequisites: Sign in with edit access to facility groups.
Use the correct organization/location details for the facility group.
steps: Open Facility Group and choose its add action, or select an existing group to edit.
Complete Facility Group Name, Facility Group Name Arabic, Country, State, City, and Phone Office 1; these are required.
Optionally enter Email Address, Website URL, other contact details, and active state.
Select Save and review the validation or success response.
notes: Country, State, and City are dependent choices. Phone Office 1 is numeric and has length validation.
This record provides a parent grouping for facilities and service configuration; specific options shown may depend on configured lookups and permissions.

title: Set up a facility and manage its settings
prerequisites: Create or identify the facility group first.
Sign in with permission to edit facilities; setting edit controls may be hidden without it.
steps: Open Facility and choose the add action, or select a facility to edit.
In Facility Details, complete Facility Group, Facility Name, Facility Name Arabic, Country, State, City, Phone Office 1, Facility Address, and Facility Address Arabic; these are required.
Optionally add legal/contact details and a facility logo (the picker accepts image files); use the preview and Remove control to inspect or clear a selected logo.
Open the Settings tab to review existing settings. If allowed, use Add Setting, complete Category, Data Type, Setting Key, Placeholder, and the type-specific Setting Value, then save.
Use Save Settings after changing existing settings; return to the facility form's Save action to save facility details.
notes: Facility Name and location are mandatory. Editing an existing facility can lock its Facility Group; setting availability and fields are configuration/permission dependent.
Settings are rendered from facility-specific records and data types (including boolean and file settings); the screen does not define a universal list of setting keys.
The Settings panel is embedded in the manage-facility experience; there is no separate active facility-settings route in PayerRoutingModule.
Do not use the facility logo upload as a claim/payment attachment workflow.

title: Create or update a facility clinic
prerequisites: Create the facility group and facility first.
Sign in with permission to maintain clinics.
steps: Open Clinic and select its add action, or choose an existing clinic to edit.
Select Facility Group and Facility, then enter Clinic Name, Clinic Name Arabic, and External Code; these are required.
Set Active if the clinic should be active.
Select Save and review any validation message before returning to the clinic list.
notes: Facility Group and Facility are locked for an existing clinic. Facility options depend on the selected group.
The available fields and access are configuration-dependent; no downstream payer contract behavior is inferred.

title: Set up a facility doctor and license records
prerequisites: Create the facility group and facility first.
Sign in with permission to maintain doctor profiles.
steps: Open Doctor and select its add action, or edit an existing doctor.
Select Facility Group and Facility; then complete Doctor Name, Nationality, Gender, Date of Birth, Date of Joining, and External Code.
Complete the required license and login fields shown by the form, including License Type and License Expiry Date, and add license-row data when required.
Review the form's validation messages, including duplicate license-type validation where shown, then select Save.
notes: Facility is required and becomes locked on existing doctor records. Doctor Name, Nationality, Gender, Date of Birth, Date of Joining, External Code, License Type, License Expiry Date, and Doctor Login are required by the current form model.
Additional fields, lookup options, and field-level permission can be configuration-dependent; do not invent a doctor-to-claims assignment workflow.

title: Build the facility service category and group hierarchy
prerequisites: Create or identify the facility group that owns the service structure.
Sign in with the required setup permissions.
steps: Start with Service Category: choose a Facility Group and enter Service Category Name, Service Category Name Arabic, Service Category Code, and External Code; all are required.
Create a Service Group for that facility group with Service Group Name, Service Group Name Arabic, Service Group Code, Alias, Alias Arabic, and External Code; these fields are required.
Create a Service Sub Group for the facility group with Service Sub Group Name, Service Sub Group Name Arabic, Service Sub Group Code, and External Code; these fields are required.
Set Active as appropriate on each record, select Save, and check the list screen for the saved entries.
notes: Each add/edit form has a Facility Group selector; existing child records may lock their group. Use the setup hierarchy and options supplied by the UI rather than assuming a data relationship beyond those fields.
The screens provide list and add/edit routes, but specific row-level actions may vary by permissions.

title: Search and maintain service catalog entries
prerequisites: Set up the facility group and service hierarchy first.
Sign in with permission to view or update the service catalog.
steps: On Service Catalog, optionally filter by Facility Group, Service Category, or External Code and select Search.
Use the add action or open an existing entry to manage it.
For a new entry, choose Facility Group, Service Category, Service Group, and Service Sub Group in order, then complete Service Catalog Name and Service Catalog Name Arabic.

Complete the required catalog price and service attributes shown for the selected record, including Gender and any required numeric/service-code rows; select standard-code lookup controls when available.
Select Save and review the returned status.
notes: When editing, the hierarchy selectors are disabled. The form has additional validation for numeric price/code and row-level values; follow the validation displayed for the specific entry.

An Update Claims control is rendered by the generic buttons with a legacy Nphies type input; whether this is enabled depends on configuration and permission. Do not infer it syncs an external payer successfully.
The list's search filters are Facility Group, Service Category, and External Code; Service Group and Service Sub Group controls are currently commented out on that list template.

title: Run and export the unclaimed detail report
prerequisites: Sign in with report access.
Choose a reporting period; date controls are mandatory.
steps: Set From Date and To Date; both are required. The initial result period is the previous calendar month.
Optionally filter by Facility Group and Facility, and select a Payer and related Policy.
Select Search to load the detail table.
Use the table's CSV, Excel, PDF, or Print export control when present.
notes: Facility and payer/policy lookup options are loaded by the screen; the policy selector is refreshed for the selected payer.
The detail table includes claim and patient identifiers plus gross/net, discount, deductible, and reimbursement amounts; handle exported data under your organization's healthcare-data controls.
Export availability and report results depend on configured data and permissions.

title: Run and export the unclaimed summary report
prerequisites: Sign in with report access.
steps: Set required From Date and To Date; the initial range is the previous calendar month.
Optionally choose Facility Group and Facility, Payer, and a Policy associated with that payer.
Select Search to refresh the summary table.
Use the table's available export controls to save or print the displayed report.
notes: Changing Facility Group reloads the facility list; changing Payer clears and reloads the policy list.
The date and other filters are passed to the report service; no result is guaranteed when matching data is absent or service access fails.

title: Run claimed claim detail or summary reports
prerequisites: Sign in with report access.
Use a reporting range with both dates entered.
steps: Choose the appropriate route for Claimed Detail or Claimed Summary.
Set required From Date and To Date; the screens initialize to the previous calendar month.
Optionally select Facility Group and Facility, Payer, and the associated Policy.
Select Search to reload the report table.
Use the displayed table's export controls (CSV, Excel, PDF, or Print where present) for the returned rows.
notes: Facility and policy choices are dependent on their selected parent filters. The detail screen returns claim-level rows; the summary screen groups claims and totals by payer.
Only the From Date and To Date fields are required by the form model; other displayed filters may be left blank.
Treat downloaded patient/claim-level output as sensitive data and export only as permitted by local policy.

title: Run payer-, doctor-, or clinic-wise rejection reports
prerequisites: Sign in with report access.
Select both report dates.
steps: Open the payer-wise, doctor-wise, or clinic-wise rejection report route.
Set From Date and To Date; optionally select Facility Group, Facility, Payer, and the Policy associated with the selected payer.
Select Search to load the rejection results.
Use the on-screen table export controls to export or print the displayed results.
notes: From Date and To Date are required. The three reports share date and facility/payer/policy filters; results are grouped by payer, doctor, or clinic according to the selected route.
The filter labels and report values are supplied by the UI and service; no specific rejection cause or data availability is assumed.
Downloaded rejection data may contain sensitive claim information.

title: Search reports and grant report access
prerequisites: Sign in with report-administration access; available actions depend on assigned report permissions.
steps: Open Reports and use Search to narrow the list by report Name or Data API name.
Select Add New to open report creation, or use Edit or Delete on a row when those actions are available.
Select Grant Access for a report and choose one or more Users in the dialog.
Select Save in the Grant Access dialog, then check the response.
notes: The list includes report Name, Data API name, and paginated rows. Add New and Edit are permission-gated; the view also contains a Delete action.
The Grant Access modal's selectable users/groups are lookup-provided; the report record can also be edited in the report designer.
Do not assume that a grant enables all report actions; viewing/downloading rights are represented separately in report access data.

title: Create or edit a configured report
prerequisites: Sign in with report New/Edit permission.
For editing, navigate from an existing report row so the report ID is carried in navigation state.
Use a backend-supported Data API name; validation is performed by the application.
steps: Select Type, enter Name, and enter Data API Name; these fields are required.
Select the validate action beside Data API Name before building filters.

When filters are available, use Add Filters. For each filter, enter Title and choose Type and Entity; choose Condition for number/date range filters, and set Is Mandatory or Is OR Selector if appropriate.
Optionally mark the report Request Based and use Open Designer to configure the report template.
Save through the designer's save control and review the success or validation response.
notes: Supported UI filter types include text, number, datetime, selector, and multiselect; the Designer offers equal/range field conditions.

Report validation, available entities/columns, filter APIs, and designer controls depend on backend configuration. Do not invent a universal report endpoint or assert that an arbitrary Data API name will work.
The Report Designer constructor redirects to the report list if an edit navigation state lacks a report ID.

title: View, filter, favorite, or download a report
prerequisites: Sign in with access to My Reports.
The report must be available to the current user, and the corresponding view/download access must be granted.
steps: Select a report from the available report list.
Complete required report filters marked with an asterisk; select from configured list controls or enter the required values.
Select View when it is available. To export, select Download and choose an offered format such as Excel, PDF, or CSV; HTML is offered for non-request-based reports.
Select Make Favorite or Un-Favorite in the filter panel to add or remove a non-request-based report from favorites.
notes: Filters and output formats vary by report definition. The shared viewer loads configured columns and template and checks report access; required filters are enforced by the generated form.
A report with no filters may run immediately when its template loads.
View and download availability can differ by user/group grant; a visible report does not imply download permission.

title: Run general reports and track requested reports
prerequisites: Sign in with access to My Reports.
Report categories and available reports depend on user grants and report configuration.
steps: In General Reports, search by report name and choose a Report Type, then select a listed report.
Complete required filters in the report viewer. Use View to display it, or Download to choose an offered output format.
For long-running reports, switch to Requested Reports, choose the relevant report category/name, and select Request Report in the report viewer.
Use Refresh to reload Requested Reports History. When the request is complete, use its View or Download action when available.
notes: The two tabs separate non-request-based reports from request-based reports. Results, formats, and filter requirements vary by definition.
The UI shows Pending when a request lacks a file path or has pending status and may auto-poll every 10 seconds while pending.
A displayed completion/file link does not guarantee the artifact is reachable; backend generation and storage access are environment-dependent.

title: Assign report view and download access
prerequisites: Open the screen with report-administration permission.
Select the relevant role or user context; available entries depend on configuration.
steps: Choose Roles to view the access assignments for that role.
Select Users where applicable, then set the View and Download access checkboxes for the displayed assignments.
Remove an assignment with its Remove action only when appropriate.
Select Save and review the confirmation or error response.
notes: The access-management form exposes separate View and Download flags. Assignments may include role- and user-level entries, and canDownload is not implied by canView.
Available roles/users and whether the screen permits edits are permission/configuration dependent.
